opencode-grok-usage

Live Grok usage in the OpenCode V2 sidebar — SuperGrok weekly credits or xAI API rate limits.
A small standalone plugin: server RPC + TUI panel + grok_usage tool.

> [!WARNING] > **Unofficial and not affiliated with xAI.** The subscription mode reads the > billing endpoints used by the Grok CLI and grok.com. Those are undocumented, > can change at any time, and using them may violate xAI's terms. Use your own > account at your own risk. The API mode uses the official xAI API and > Management API. Read [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md). ## What it shows | Mode | Data | Source | | --- | --- | --- | | **Subscription** (SuperGrok / X Premium+) | Weekly credit usage %, reset time, per-product breakdown, monthly dollar allowance, on-demand/prepaid balance | `cli-chat-proxy.grok.com/v1/billing` with the xAI login stored in OpenCode, or `~/.grok/auth.json` | | **API** (`XAI_API_KEY`) | Requests/tokens rate-limit remaining, optional prepaid balance | `api.x.ai/v1/models` rate-limit headers; Management API balance | `auto` mode prefers the xAI login already stored in OpenCode, then a Grok CLI login, then `XAI_API_KEY`. ## Prerequisites - OpenCode **2.x**. - Node **22.18+** for the helper CLI. - One of: - **OpenCode xAI login** (this is what a running Grok session already uses): `opencode auth login`, then choose xAI → SuperGrok Subscription. - **Grok CLI login**: install the Grok CLI, run `grok login`, and keep `~/.grok/auth.json`. - **API key**: `XAI_API_KEY` on the OpenCode server, or an xAI API key saved in OpenCode. - Optional for balance: `XAI_MANAGEMENT_KEY` and `XAI_TEAM_ID`. ## Install ```bash git clone https://github.com/officialPlocki/opencode-grok-usage.git ~/.local/share/opencode-grok-usage-src cd ~/.local/share/opencode-grok-usage-src npm install --omit=dev ``` Add it to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": [ { "package": "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-grok-usage-src", "options": { "mode": "auto" } } ] } ``` Reload (`/reload`). The panel appears when an `xai/...` model is selected. > [!NOTE] > OpenCode caches plugin modules by path. After updating, install into a > versioned directory (`npm run install:local`) or restart the service. ## Usage ```text /grok-status # detailed report /grok-refresh # bypass the 30 s cache ``` The `grok_usage` tool exposes the same data to agents. ### Sidebar Subscription: ```text GROK USAGE SuperGrok · weekly ██████ 11% used reset Fri 09:34 $29.31 / $150.00 month ``` API: ```text GROK USAGE xAI API req 119/120 tok 4.2M/5M balance $10.00 ``` The panel is only shown while an xAI model is selected. Set `alwaysShow: true` to keep it visible for every model. ## Authentication ### Subscription OpenCode stores a SuperGrok login in its own credential store, not in `~/.grok/auth.json`. The plugin reads the active `xai` connection (`ctx.integration.connection`) and, if that is unavailable, the same row in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`. Expired grants are refreshed with the client id already inside the access token. A rotated refresh token is written back to that row so OpenCode keeps working. Disable the write-back with `refreshTokens: false`. A Grok CLI login is still accepted. The plugin reads the first usable entry from `~/.grok/auth.json` (or `GROK_AUTH_FILE`) when that file exists: ```json { "entry-id": { "key": "", "refresh_token": "", "expires_at": "2026-11-09T12:00:00.000Z", "email": "you@example.com", "oidc_issuer": "https://auth.x.ai", "oidc_client_id": "" } } ``` Expired tokens are refreshed through the issuer's OIDC discovery. Refreshed tokens are written back to the file with mode `0600` so the Grok CLI stays in sync. Disable the write-back with `refreshTokens: false`. For CI or a custom login, set `GROK_ACCESS_TOKEN` and skip the file entirely. ### API Set `XAI_API_KEY` on the OpenCode server: ```bash XAI_API_KEY=xai-... opencode --standalone ``` For the shared service: ```bash opencode service set env XAI_API_KEY xai-... ``` Optional balance (official Management API): ```bash XAI_MANAGEMENT_KEY=... XAI_TEAM_ID=... ``` ## Options ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "/home/you/.local/share/opencode-grok-usage-src", "options": { "mode": "auto", "pollMs": 30000, "refreshTokens": true, "alwaysShow": false } } ] } ``` | Option | Default | Meaning | | --- | --- | --- | | `mode` | `auto` | `auto`, `subscription`, or `api` | | `authFile` | `~/.grok/auth.json` | Alternative credential file | | `refreshTokens` | `true` | Persist refreshed OIDC tokens back to the file | | `pollMs` | `30000` | TUI poll interval (minimum 10 s); server cache is 30 s | | `alwaysShow` | `false` | Show the panel for every model, not just xAI | | `teamId` | `XAI_TEAM_ID` | Team for the prepaid balance | Environment: `GROK_AUTH_FILE`, `GROK_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `XAI_API_KEY`, `XAI_MANAGEMENT_KEY`, `XAI_TEAM_ID`. ## How it works ``` OpenCode TUI ──RPC (30 s)──▶ server plugin ──▶ cli-chat-proxy.grok.com │ or api.x.ai ├─ OpenCode xAI connection (SuperGrok) └─ ~/.grok/auth.json (optional CLI login) ``` - Tokens never leave the local server; the RPC returns usage only. - No analytics, no third-party relays. - Subscription requests send `x-grok-client-mode: cli`, the header the Grok CLI uses for its billing call. - The Management API balance ledger is inverted (a top-up appears negative); the plugin displays the absolute cent value. ## Troubleshooting | Symptom | Fix | | --- | --- | | `No Grok login found` | Connect xAI in OpenCode (`opencode auth login`), run `grok login`, or set `GROK_ACCESS_TOKEN` | | `Grok rejected the token` | Re-run `grok login`; the refresh token was revoked | | No API numbers | `XAI_API_KEY` missing or the server has no rate-limit headers | | Panel missing | Select an `xai/...` model, or set `alwaysShow: true` | | `balance` wrong | Management balance parsing is best-effort; verify in the xAI console | ## Development ```bash npm install npm test npm run typecheck npm run install:local ``` Tests cover auth file parsing, OIDC refresh, billing shapes, balance extraction and options. No network is used. ## Legal The subscription mode uses an undocumented billing endpoint. It is not affiliated with xAI and may stop working or violate their terms. The API mode uses the official xAI API. See [`LEGAL.md`](LEGAL.md) for the full notice. ## License MIT — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE).

# User information and risk notice

This page explains what this plugin does, what it needs, and what can happen
when you use it. It is written for users, not as legal advice, and it is **not
legal advice**. xAI's terms and your local law always take precedence.

## What this software does

`opencode-grok-usage` displays Grok usage in OpenCode. It supports two sources:

* **Subscription mode** reads the billing endpoints used by the Grok CLI and
  grok.com, authenticated with the xAI login already stored in OpenCode or the
  OIDC token in `~/.grok/auth.json`.
* **API mode** reads the official xAI API rate-limit headers and, optionally,
  the prepaid balance from the xAI Management API.

The plugin only reads usage. It does not send prompts, proxy model requests or
modify your Grok account.

## What you need

* Your **own** account. Do not use credentials you are not allowed to use.
* A local xAI login in OpenCode, a Grok CLI login (`grok login`), or `XAI_API_KEY`.
* Optional: a management key and team id for the prepaid balance.

## What xAI may do

* The subscription billing endpoint is undocumented; it can change or disappear.
* Using it may violate xAI's terms and could affect your account.
* Rate limits and billing formats can change without notice.
* The plugin may report wrong numbers if a response shape changes.

## Your responsibility

* Comply with xAI's terms and applicable law.
* Keep `~/.grok/auth.json` private (mode `0600`).
* Do not use the plugin to scrape, resell or bypass limits for others.
* Use an unofficial integration at your own risk.

## Privacy and security

* No analytics, no telemetry, no third-party relays.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

The current `0.1.x` line receives fixes.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Report security issues privately through a GitHub security advisory on the
repository. Do not open a public issue for credential leaks or auth bypasses.

## Credential handling

* Subscription tokens are read from the active OpenCode xAI connection, from
  OpenCode's local credential database, or from `~/.grok/auth.json` (or
  `GROK_AUTH_FILE` / `GROK_ACCESS_TOKEN`).
* Refreshed CLI tokens are written back to the auth file with mode `0600`.
  Refreshed OpenCode grants are written back to the same credential row.
  Disable either write-back with `refreshTokens: false`.
* Tokens are never returned by the plugin RPC and never leave the local server.
* API keys are read from the server environment (`XAI_API_KEY`,
  `XAI_MANAGEMENT_KEY`) and only sent to `api.x.ai` / `management-api.x.ai`.
* No analytics or telemetry code exists.

## Scope

Reports about xAI's service behaviour, billing formats or account eligibility
are not vulnerabilities in this project.
